producer_report.summary: The producer's build directory is now removed before the first check starts, and a failed check keeps the last 200 lines of its output. The drain log's `checks` line now names the failing tests. Root cause: `target/produce` was removed only after every check passed, so a job held two full builds during the checks. A failed check kept only its last 4096 bytes, which often cut off the failing test. The removal helper is in run/checks.rs and is called from `check_and_verify` in run/mod.rs, which is where the `checks     ` line is built. It uses the existing `StateDir::remove_produce`, so no new deletion logic. The removal sits after the disk check that runs before the checks, so the low-disk hold tests still see the directory there. It runs whether the checks then pass or fail, and also for nested runs, as before. The candidate and its tree are untouched. A failed run's `output_tail` in the verification record (the existing field, so no new record type) is now its last 200 lines, with a 64 KiB ceiling that keeps the end. A passing run keeps 4 KiB. The log entry reads `name FAILED: a, b, +N more`. Names come from the recorded `failed_tests`, else from `test <name> ... FAILED` lines, else just the check name. `failed_tests` is not changed, so verdict logic is unaffected. The new tests in run/tests.rs and the unit tests in core checks.rs pass, and so do the existing tests in tests/drain.rs.

open_issues: run/mod.rs and run/tests.rs changed although they are not in the brief's file list. The log line, the removal point and the old kept-on-failure test are there, so the change could not stay in the listed files.
A failed check's baseline record also keeps 200 lines now, because the baseline uses the same `run_check`. This is bounded by the 64 KiB ceiling and the verdict logic does not read `output_tail`.
Because the build is removed before the checks, a send-back to the producer after a failed check rebuilds cold. The old behaviour kept the build for that case. The brief asked for this tradeoff.
The 64 KiB ceiling could cut a 200-line tail whose lines are very long, so the tail would then be shorter than 200 lines. A unit test covers this case.
mistakes: My first unit test asserted a 250-line passing run is cut by bytes, but its output was only about 2.2 KB. I changed the script to 600 lines and the test passed.

I first put the removal only in the non-nested, non-resumed branch. That would have left a nested run's build in place, which the old code removed. I moved it to just after the stage entry so nested runs are covered too.
learnings: The `checks     <name> FAILED (..s)` log line is built in `check_and_verify` in crates/athena-core/src/run/mod.rs. crates/athena-cli/src/drain.rs prints no check lines.

`CheckRun.output_tail` is read only by introspect.rs and reading.rs, which clip it themselves, and by the baseline tail test in crates/athena-cli/tests/lifecycle.rs. That test still holds, since a failed 600-line run keeps 200 short lines (about 2.2 KB).
The baseline also runs the checks, so a test check that fails on both base and candidate is marked pre-existing and can still land. The failing-check test therefore fails only on the edited README.
Bash for the producer allows no pipes, so `| tail` is blocked and long cargo output has to be read whole.
